docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. In Edit > Preferences > Get Extentions Search for "Surface Psycho", click Install.

  2. In Edit > Preferences > Add-ons > SurfacePsycho click Add assets path

More details on installation and setup here

docs.title: Start designing
docs.text:
1. Add a SurfacePsycho object : Shift+A > Surface, or Shift+A > Curve and select one in the bottom section. Understand what SP objects are here

  2. Tab to get in edit mode. SP objects are simply mesh objects with specific attributes. You can edit it like any mesh More details here

  3. Add modifiers for non-destructive editing. If you have setup the library correctly, SP modifiers should appear in the modifier list under SurfacePsycho sub-menu. More details here

docs.title: Export your design
docs.text:
Export selected SurfacePsycho objects as STEP files with N panel > SurfacePsycho > Quick export (saved in current .blend folder). More details here

  • Keymap

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text: If you encounter any issue not described below, please report it ↗️.

docs.title: "DLL not found"
docs.text:
In some still unclear configurations, the add-on fails to load with an error "DLL not found". To fix it go to your extension folder ...\Blender Foundation\Blender\X.X\extensions and delete .cache and .local folders. This will force to reinstall the external python modules.

If you encounter any issue with this procedure, please let me know.

docs.title: Add your file to the list
docs.text:
All your .blend files using SurfacePsycho are welcome. The goal is for new users to understand the logic, so the cleaner is the file the better, however do what you can, something is better than nothing so there is a high tolerance for the mess. Please put the add-on's version and Blender's version in the file name (e.g. "My spaceship v3 final final sp0.10.4-b5.2.blend")

To add a file follow these steps : 1. Click the Fork button (top right) 3. On the fork page, just click Create fork (keep the default settings) 4. You are now on your own copy of the repo. Click Add file → Upload files 5. Drag and drop your files 6. Click Commit changes at the bottom. Your files are now saved in your copy 7. Click Contribute → Open pull request 8. Give your pull request any title, then click Create pull request Done! I will review your submission and merge it into the main repository

Alternatively just join the project's Discord and share your file in the #duckumentation channel so I add them.

Also don't hesitate to put your name everywhere so people can easily thank you.

docs.title: Your data is safe
docs.text: Files using SurfacePsycho objects open without the add-on ! They are perfectly standard .blend files. No lost of data or anything. This is by design and stay the case.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text:
SP objects made with older SP versions might not export properly or connect to more recent ones. Once a new version of the add-on is installed, four operators allows you to upgrade objects:

Warning : upgrade operators are still experimental and not all exposed in the UI. To find them perform an operator search (F3 by default). In case of issue, undo and please report the issue. Also note modifiers older than 0.9.4 cannot by losslessly upgraded.

docs.title: Upgrade per Object
docs.text:
SP - Update operator replaces old modifiers by new ones for the selected objects and perform the versionning actions to preserve the shapes.

This is the safest operator yet.

docs.title: Upgrade All Node Groups
docs.text: SP - Update All Node Groups replaces globally all SP groups of the file by newer ones and perform the versionning actions to preserve the shapes.

docs.title: Upgrade Node Group
docs.text: SP - Update Node Group replaces globally one SP groups of the file by it's newer version and perform versionning actions associated to preserve the shapes.

docs.title: Replace Node Group
docs.text: SP - Replace Node Group gives additional freedom : you can replace any group by any other globaly in the file. Note it will not perform versionning actions.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
I have an old patches with modifier node group "mod", I want to convert it to the new versions. - Add a new patch with shift+A - Copy its node-group name (⚠️ can be different from the modifier name) - let's say it is called "mod.001" - copy the name - Click Replace Node Group - Paste the name into both fields and remove the ".001" of target - Click ok

If you have more versions "mod" "mod.001" "mod.002"..., the best is to rename the version you want to keep with no suffix and use ".*" suffix on the target to replace all others at once

docs.title: Add-on Structure
docs.text:
SurfacePsycho is only made of :

  • An asset library of GeometryNodes modifiers and some shapes presets
  • A CAD file importer and exporter
  • Some buttons for efficiency (N panel > Item > SurfacePsycho)

docs.title: SP - Coon Patch
docs.text:
MODIFIER

Coon patches allow to fill a square of 4 Bezier segments. Used directly on a Bezier Patch, it has two modes depending on what meshes it get as input :

  1. A grid mesh : in this case it moves the mid control points
  2. A 4-edges wire : in this case it generate the grid

(the mode is automatically selected)

docs.text: Modifies the current curve to connect to a target curve with the desired level of continuity.

docs.title: SP - Connect Flat Patch
docs.text: Connects one segment of the current Flat Patch to a target Flat Patch segment. If the target edge is straight, the patch orientation keeps a degree of freedom, otherwise it is projected on the target patch's plane.

docs.title: SP - Convert Circles and Ellipses to Splines
docs.text: Samples each circle or ellipse into a spline of approximately the same shape.

docs.title: SP - Convert Contour
docs.text: It's purpose is to give several operation for conversions of trim contours.

docs.title: Fit to UV
docs.text: Since 0.9 version, the fit option for trim contour was removed (its usage could be confusing). The idea was that it scales any trim contour to fit the natural boundaries of the patch. Fit to UV provides a way to upgrade old patches using it as well as giving you access to the old behavior if you like.

docs.title: To Normalized Knot
docs.text: Scales the trim contour of NURBS patch to fit in the range 0 to 1m while preserving the shape by scaling the knots too. This is very useful to edit an imported model. Some imported surfaces can commonly have contours ranging from 0 to 10km which make them impractical to edit.

docs.title: To NURBS
docs.text: Convert contour segments of every type to NURBS

docs.title: To Rational Beziers
docs.text: Convert contour segments of every type to Rational Beziers. This splits each span of NURBS.

docs.title: SP - Convert Flat Patch to Bezier Patch
docs.text: Any flat patch can be represented exactly by a degree 1x1 Bezier Patch with the matching trim contour. This modifier does exactly that. It allows you to further edit your patch into a non flat one.

docs.title: SP - NURBS to Bezier Curve or FlatPatch
SP - NURBS to Bezier Patches
docs.text: NURBS to Bezier splits a multi%20span NURBS patch into multiple single span (Bezier) patches. It's a compound type operation. Therefore it can only work if added to a compound object. To use it you need to choose a NURBS object as an operation target. In order to get individual Bezier patches, use explode compound on the compound object.

docs.title: SP - Raise or Lower Curve Degree

docs.title: SP - Raise or Lower Degree of Selected Segment
Ingredients
docs.text:
• 1 SP Compound object (cf. Compound object)
  • 1 SubD to Compound modifier

docs.title: Directions
docs.text:
• Add the modifier to the Compound object
  • Make sure it is above the Compound Meshing modifier
  • Any mesh you create inside the compound object is now subdivided smoothly and converted to Bezier patches
  • Adjust the subdivision level
  • ~~Serve warm, with a glass of white wine~~

If you want to edit individual patches, use explode compound

To improve editing speed, you can temporarily uncheck Compute and disable Compound Meshing. It is then equivalent to the standard Subdivision Surface modifier.

Supports creases

Ignores N-gons and triangles

Not yet accurate and precisely continuous

docs.title: Usage example
docs.text:
You have two wires you want to connect like this :

docs.title: SP - Fillet Polyline with Circles
docs.text:
Allows to create circular arcs to round corners of Curve or Flat Patch wires. It is currently limited to straight segments and ignores all the segments types.

To control the radius per corner, you can use the built-in bevel weight, however, you need to assign it manually to the factor field. Do so by using the Input Attribute Toggle button at the right of the field.

docs.title: SP - Extrude Compound
docs.text:
This modifier allow to extrude curves or flat patches in a specified direction. The extrusion result has several surfaces, meaning the modifier must be on a compound object. - The extruded curve or flat patch can either be from a separate object target, or from the mesh of the compound itself (Extrude Self option), in which case no target is required. - The direction and length of the extrusion are either controlled by the Direction and Offset parameters or by an edge in the mesh if Use Vertices as Offset is enabled.

docs.text:
Normals generated by default are bent at the border. You can fix this issue by enabling "Exact Normal" (disabled by default because of poor performances).

docs.title: SP - Surface of Extrusion Meshing
docs.text:
MODIFIER MESHING

To mesh surfaces of extrusion. Extrusion surfaces are a separate type in the STEP norm. Part of the benefit of using them compared to just a ruled surface (degree 1 in the extrusion direction), is that you can extrude any type of segment (circles, ellipses...).

docs.title: SP - Surface of Revolution Meshing
docs.text:
MODIFIER MESHING

To mesh surfaces of revolution. It takes as input a first edge which defines the axis of symmetry and a second mesh island which is the control geometry of the segment to revolve. Revolution less than 360° are done through trimming (in accordance to the STEP norm). A modifier have been added to make the operation easier : SP - Adjust Revolution Sweep Angle

docs.text:
Used to contrain control points to keep the patches symmetric. Typically used for a car hood or roof to maintain continuity when passing through the mirror plane. It acts only on the positions of existing control points and don't add new ones.

If you are looking for classic mesh symmetry, use the default mirror modifier

Currently only supported for Bezier surfaces, or NURBS with automatic knots.

docs.title: Curves
docs.text: To display the curvature of a curve at every evaluated point, enable curvature combs in the mesher modifier.

docs.title: Surfaces
docs.text: For surfaces, there is a specific modifier: SP - Curvature Analysis. It can be added automatically to every surfaces through N Panel > SurfacePsycho > View > Curvature Analysis. By default it displays the mean curvature

docs.title: Matcaps
docs.text: To register the matcaps shiped with the addon, go to Edit > Preferences > Add-ons > SurfacePsycho > Psycho Matcaps and click Add. They will appear in the matcap list. For better analysis, increase surfaces resolutions, enable Exact Normals and EEVEE's high quality normals (More info here).

docs.text: Use SP - Plot Distance Between Curve

docs.title: Add Control Points
docs.text: Use loop cuts and extrusions (Ctrl+R and E)

docs.title: Remove Control Points
docs.text: Use dissolve (Shift+X)

docs.title: Edit Wires
docs.text: A wire is a chain of segments. To create one, in mesh editing you need to create a chain of vertices connected by edges. They represent the control points of the wire. Editing wires is then the same as editing a standard mesh plus assigning some attributes. By default, the chain represents a single Bezier segment (or a cyclic B-spline if closed).

docs.title: Editing panel
docs.text: N panel > SurfacePsycho tab > Edit section in edit mode, gives you access to all the wire specific actions and properties.

docs.title: Segment pie menu
docs.text: Some properties are more accessible with Shift + F pie menu, the shortcut only works if the SP Mode is enabled (in edit mode).

docs.title: Split into segments
docs.text: For your wire to have several segment, each segment must be delimited by Endpoints.

docs.title: Display Endpoints
docs.text: In edit mode, enabling the SP Mode tool in the left toolbar highlights vertices assigned as endpoints with black squares.

docs.title: Assign and unassign Endpoints
docs.text: To assign selected vertices as endpoints, use Shift + F + Drag down or from the panel Endpoints > Toggle. Both methods toggle the endpoint status, so to unassign, just do it again (the active vertex status decides which action to perform).

docs.title: Change Segment Type
docs.text: Again from the pie menu or the panel, you have a all the supported segment types (all types supported by the STEP format). To assign a type to a segment, select it's first point and select a type. An important current limitation is that you cannot differentiate between the first and last point. The best for the moment is then to test both and undo the wrong one :/

docs.title: Change Segment resolution
docs.text: Select the first point of a segment, go to the panel and change the values of Segment Resolution property.

docs.title: Change Segment Degree
docs.text: Select the first point of a segment, go to the panel and change the values of NURBS Degree property. You can also change the degree from the pie menu by dragging up on Spline and use the mouse wheel to change the degree.

docs.title: Set Weight
docs.text: To change the weight of control points, select them and go to the panel and change the values of Weight property. An important limitation is that currently an endpoint shared between two segment cannot have 2 different weights assigned.

docs.title: Exact Normals
docs.text:
By default SP doesn't calculate accurate normals on NURBS and Bezier patches because it has a significant performance cost. However you can switch it on per object, from the N panel or from the meshing modifier. Most the difference is on boundaries.

For further quality you can enable EEVEE high quality normals

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text: Default Exact Exact + High Quality

docs.title: Explode Compound
docs.text:
Operator to split each shape of the selected compound object to a separated object.

Useful to edit individual shapes afterward.

docs.title: Import
docs.text: Import any CAD file with File > Import > SurfacePsycho CAD (.step, .iges). The importer is still in progress. Expect variable quality. Also note that the importer doesn't preserve any B-rep connections, it creates the surfaces and curves as individual objects.

docs.title: Export
docs.text: SurfacePsycho proposes three export formats : .step, .iges and .svg.

docs.title: .STEP
docs.text:
File > Export > SurfacePsycho STEP (.step)

This will export the selected SP objects. The exporter directly performs sewing

docs.title: Quick export
docs.text: Button in N panel > SurfacePsycho > Quick export. Quick exports in the current blend file folder. If the blend file never been saved : it saves at the path specified in Edit > Preferences > File Paths > Temporary File.

docs.title: .IGES
docs.text:
File > Export > SurfacePsycho IGES (.iges)

The ancestor of step. Here because it costs nothing. Essentially like STEP but with less features.

docs.title: .SVG
docs.text:
File > Export > SurfacePsycho SVG (.svg) Implemented to allow designers to make logo and UI's directly on the product surface. Since svg only support straight lines and cubic beziers, objects must have the following modifier for conversion SP - Make SVG Ready

Note : All the other native exporters are also supported but will export standard meshes

docs.title: Instancing
docs.text:
Surface Psycho supports collection instances at export. Important however, it currently have certain restrictions:

  • No negative scaling
  • No nesting

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: To non destructively edit SP objects : * Drag and drop a modifier from the asset library onto the object to edit or search for it in the modifier list * Reorder the stack to your liking (top one is applied first) * Set its parameters

docs.title: Meshing Modifiers
docs.text: Each SP object must have a Meshing modifiers to be evaluated as a STEP shape. There is one for each object type (see object types). The meshing modifier must be the last one editing the shape. Modifiers before the meshing modifier act on the control geometry. Some modifiers are however made to come after : - Mirror - Any other viewer/analysis modifier

docs.title: Compatible default Blender modifiers
docs.text:
• Any deform modifier (which do not modify vertex indexing) works in part 1 of the stack (e.g. Displace modifier). It simply deforms the control geometry. You can also use an Array modifier then a Weld modifier on a Curve object

  • Mirror modifier : Because symmetry is important in product design, standard mirror is supported on all entities. Important to note however :

  • the mirror modifier(s) needs to be placed last
  • Merge option can cause issues at export

  • Bisect and UV settings are not supported

  • Array modifier : Works for compounds but just the first shape of the compound

docs.title: Must know
docs.text:
1. Every SP object can support your own GeometryNodes modifiers, but each object is limited to a single shape except for Compounds. Make a compound to start: Shift+A>Surface>Compound
  2. Add a GeometryNodes modifier to it (necessarily on top of the compound meshing modifier), create a new node group and edit the node tree.
  3. GeometryNodes compatible with SP must have the following :
  4. The output must be made only of instances with a shape type attribute (on the instance domain).
  5. To add it, use a SP - Set Patch Instance Type node group on your instances and select your desired type.
  6. Each shape instance must contain exactly what other SP object meshes contain : Some control geometry with some attributes on it

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Look at pre-made shapes in the assets. They are examples for how to make procedural setups.
  • Use vertices indices to select and move them
  • SP - Grid coordinates node gives you the row and column index of points

docs.title: SP Mode
docs.text:
From the left tool-bar in Object mode and Edit mode, you can activate the SP Mode Tool

The enabled, it gives you several overlays and shortcuts to speedup your workflow :

docs.title: Segment Selection
docs.text:
• In Object mode, segments are highlighted at cursor hover. Selected one by pressing Ctrl+Left Click. Select more by using Ctrl+Shift+Left Click.
  • In Edit mode, vertices tagged as Endpoints are shown with a black square.

docs.title: Keymap
docs.text: A specific keymap is toggled by the tool. It tries to minimize overlaps with Blender default keys you usually need for surface editing.

docs.title: Add
docs.text: Add SP objects from the add menu shift+A > Surface, shift+A > Curve or from the asset library

docs.title: What they are
docs.text:
• Under the hood SurfacePsycho compatible objects are simply Blender objects which stores the right attributes. a
  • Most of the time, it is a mesh object with a Meshing Modifier
  • The meshing modifier provides the attributes required for the exporter to read and for interaction between objects
  • New SP objects can be made from scratch by adding a meshing modifier to any mesh

docs.title: Types
docs.text: Entity Icon & color Entity Icon & color Entity Icon & color NURBS Patch Flat Patch Bezier Patch Curve Compound Others ICON TO ADD

docs.title: Curve
docs.text: A curve object contains a single wire. Requires a Curve Meshing modifier. Default Blender curves cannot be exported with SP directly, but they can be converted with SP - Copy Internal Curve.

docs.title: FlatPatch
docs.text: Planar surfaces built from a set of wires. Theses wires are flatten to either the object XY plane or to mean plane if Orient option is enabled. Requires a FlatPatch Meshing modifier

docs.title: NURBS Patch
docs.text: Your typical Non-Uniform-Rational-B-Spline. Requires a NURBS Patch Meshing modifier

docs.title: Bezier Patch
docs.text: Single span NURBS patch. The 2 reason for the separation is that they are faster and simpler to work with. As a consequence a lot of algorithm are implemented on them at first, and ported to NURBS later. Requires a Bezier Patch Meshing modifier

docs.title: Compound
docs.text: An object containing several SP shapes. Can be used for procedural modeling. Requires a Compound Meshing modifier

docs.title: Wire
docs.text: A single chain of vertices (open or closed) used to represent a chain of segments. To edit them see Editing Wires

docs.title: Segments
docs.text: Represent patch edges, or any curve piece with a single geometrical definition. A modifier which has a segment target can take it from any patch or curve.

docs.title: Add a Trim Contour
docs.text: To quickly add a trim contour N Panel > SurfacePsycho > Edit > Trim Contour > Add :

docs.title: Edit it
docs.text:
Trim contours in SurfacePsycho are defined with the wire system. The wires are projected over the X-Y plane of the object (X represents U, Y represents V). The trim contour is simply some geometry marked as such.

To mark or unmark some, N Panel > SurfacePsycho > Edit > Trim Contour > Toggle.

The Select button allows you to view what is already assigned.

docs.title: Non-Destructive Trimming
docs.text: Trimming surfaces can be automated by modifiers of the trim category. Note that SP - Crop or Extend Patch acts on the control points of the surface and not on its trim contour.

docs.title: Duplicate-Apply
docs.text:
• When some functions you need don't exist, you often want to manually edit the control grid. Since you don't want to lose your modifier stack here is a helpful pattern :
  • Duplicate the modifier you want to apply (Shift+D)
  • Apply one copy (Shift+A)
  • Disable the other one You can now edit the result of modifiers and, if needed, reset to previous state by re-enabling the disabled modifier.

docs.title: Generic mesh editing
docs.text: SP workflow can benefit from many add-ons and built-in tools : * EdgeFlow addon * LoopTools addon (Shipped with Blender) * The sculpt mode and proportional editing * Collection instancing

docs.title: Customize your functions
docs.text: If you know some GeometryNodes, do not hesitate to modify and reuse the node groups to your liking. GeometryNodes makes it relatively easy to understand some of the logic (by disabling and re enabling some groups and look at the result for example). A hint is that the logic very often relies on vertices indices of the control geometries. Also "SP - Grid coordinates" node gives you the row and column of points.
